newsitem.title: INDIA: Fergie in India in quest of holistic liberation.
newsitem.headline: Fergie in India in quest of holistic liberation.

text.p: British royal Sarah Ferguson has slipped into India for a secret tryst with a holistic healer, and travelled with him on Thursday to an audience with a prominent godman.

A local newspaper in the southern city of Bangalore said the Duchess of York, or Fergie as she has been dubbed by Britain's tabloid press, was being treated by homeopath and holistic healer Dr Issac Mathai who runs a clinic there.
A doctor at the clinic confirmed Fergie was in town but refused to disclose what ailment she was being treated for.
"For all details you must talk to Dr Mathai," said Dr Sudha.
Mathai and Fergie were reported to be driving down to Puttaparthi, in the neighbouring state of Andhra Pradesh, for an audience with godman Sai Baba.

"Fergie is a very down to earth, very straightforward and a spiritually attuned person. I can't relate the woman I know to the wild creature portrayed in the tabloid press," one newspaper quoted Mathai as saying.
The newspaper said Fergie was on an Indian vegetarian diet.

It said Mathai, who consults in Britain and the United States, is building a holistic centre outside Bangalore and counts celebrities like ex-Beatle George Harrison and singer Sting among his clients.
Police in Bangalore said Fergie's visit was personal and has only ventured unrecognised out of her hotel to shop.
"We are not aware of her trip here. It is a private visit. She must have come here as a commoner as nobody has asked us for security," Additional Police Commissioner T. Jayprakash told Reuters.

Earlier this month in the space of a week in the United States, Fergie signed high-priced deals to hawk cranberry juice on television and be a spokeswoman for Weight Watchers International, the programme she credited for helping her slim down.

"The media once dubbed me 'Great Fun Fergie,' saying 'She's a breath of Fresh Air,' then it was 'Round Fergie,' then 'Fat Fergie,' which gave way to 'Fat and Appalling Fergie' and then ultimately, my favourite, 'the Duchess of Pork,'" she told reporters at a Weight Watchers news conference.
